seasonRead.headline: 2011–12: Rush creation leads; the support jobs are defensive
paragraphs: Rush / Transition Chance Creator reads as the primary offensive lane: shot volume and extended attacking sequences with less of the profile devoted to physical work.

Shot-Blocking Contact Specialist is better understood as defensive detail than pure contact, while High-Touch Risk/Reward Scorer carries more puck and creation risk. That division gives a coach three distinct tools—pace, recovery work and high-touch offense—rather than one generic forward type.

seasonRead.headline: 2011–12: Pressure matters only if the next pass works
paragraphs: Puck-Pressure Transition Defenseman leads a genuinely plural blue-line map. Its takeaway and continuation signals suggest defenders whose value proposition begins with recovering the puck and doing something useful with the next touch.

Shot-Blocking Defensive Defenseman absorbs more shooting-lane work, while Offensive Puck-Moving Defenseman adds creation from the back end. Together they form a recognizable pairing architecture: recover, protect, then advance.
